transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m just tired all the time. Even by midmorning at work, after reviewing files or walking a junior adjuster through a claim, I feel like my body and my brain are already running on empty.
How long have you been feeling this tiredness?

It’s been about three years now… a little over that, maybe three years and three months. It started around when I was moved into a higher-responsibility role, mentoring other adjusters and helping oversee the new workflow systems.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed during this time?

Yes. Most days I do feel down, like there’s this gray film over everything. Even when my husband is being kind or we’re cooking with the family, I can go through the motions, but I don’t really feel the enjoyment the way I used to.
Do you find yourself losing interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yes. I still do things, like cooking with my family or spending time with my husband, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions. Most days there’s this dull, gray feeling over everything, and I don’t really enjoy things the way I used to.
Have you been feeling anxious or nervous lately?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed feeling especially nervous… not in a clear way. It’s more just how I’ve been feeling overall, but I don’t know if I’d call it anxiety.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or enjoy doing?

A little, maybe, but not like before. I still do things with my husband and family, like cooking, and I can act like I’m part of it. But most days it’s like there’s this gray film over everything, and I don’t really feel the pleasure from it the way I used to.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight over the past three years?
I haven’t really noticed any major weight change. I don’t keep very close track, but nothing stands out to me over the past few years.
Do you often feel guilty or blame yourself for things?
I don’t know… not especially. I mean, I can be hard on myself sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d say I often feel guilty or blame myself for things.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I’ve noticed a clear pattern with my sleep lately. It’s not something I’ve been keeping track of.
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find you no longer take pleasure in?

Yes. I used to paint, and I liked hiking and volunteering, but I’ve really pulled back from all of that. It’s not that I hate them now, I just don’t get much out of them, and most weeks I’m just trying to get through work and the basics. Even at work, I’m taking longer to sign off on files and missing details in audits, so by the time I’m done, I don’t have much left.
Have you ever thought about ending your life?
I don’t know… I don’t think I’ve really had thoughts about ending my life. It’s not something I’ve been planning or anything like that.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and unable to sit still?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed myself moving or talking slower than usual. And I don’t think I’ve been especially restless either, at least not enough that it stands out to me.
Do you feel like you've been fidgeting more or having trouble sitting still lately?
Not really, no. I don’t think I’ve been fidgeting more than usual, and I can sit still okay. I just haven’t noticed anything like that.
Have you noticed any changes in how quickly or slowly you're moving compared to how you used to?
No, I haven’t really noticed a change in that. I don’t think I’m moving noticeably slower or faster than I used to.
Have you felt like you're having trouble concentrating or making decisions lately?

Yes. At work, I’ve been missing details in audits that I normally would catch, and it’s taking me longer to sign off on files. Outside of work, I’ve kind of pulled back from things like painting, hiking, and volunteering because I’m mostly just trying to get through the week.
Have you experienced periods where your depressive symptoms were significantly worse than they are now?
I’m not really sure. I mean, it’s been kind of steady for a long time, so I can’t point to a clear period where it was much worse than it is now.
Have your depressive symptoms ever been significantly worse than they are now?
I don’t think so. It’s felt pretty steady to me, so I can’t really point to a time when it was clearly worse than it is now.
Have you ever had a period where you felt significantly more depressed than you do currently?

I wouldn’t say there’s been a separate period that was much worse. It’s more like most days there’s this gray film over everything. Even when my husband is being kind, or we’re cooking with the family, I can go through the motions, but I don’t really feel the enjoyment like I used to.
Have you ever felt more depressed than you do now?

Not really more than now, no. It’s more that most days feel the same—like there’s this gray film over everything. Even when my husband is kind, or we’re cooking with family, I’m there and doing it, but I don’t really feel the enjoyment like I used to.
Have you had periods where your depressive symptoms went away for a while before coming back?

No, not really. It hasn’t gone away and then come back. It’s been pretty continuous for about three years and a few months now, since I got moved into that higher-responsibility role mentoring adjusters and overseeing the new workflow systems.
